name: Ali Al Naama Coffee

We ordered a tea with lemon in a pot. We asked the order taker to add some honey for a little bit of sweetness. The order taker immediately refused.

When the pot came with I personally went to the counter and asked the waiter if we can have some honey (not for free, we are willing to pay). However, the cashier guy said I should talk to the manager.

I went to speak to the manager politely asking him if I can pay for an extra honey for our tea and the manager named Mohamed strongly said "No, it is not allowed by the Ministry. It is not allowed to drink tea and honey".

In my experience of living and dining in Qatar, I freely drink tea and honey. However, to be answered like this is very bad. If they would like to refuse a customized request the Manager could be more creative with his answer. To put the name of the Ministry on the line is so Bad that he couldn't be more accommodating to his customer.

This is a great coffee and snacks place frequented by locals. Even at 10 in the morning there was a big rush to get the food. When busy you will need to share the table with others. The correct order is to place order at the counter facing the main road followed by picking up the order at the window in the small road. You pick you tea or coffee back at the main counter by the main road. With the food and drinks you can then hunt for your table. If you have many people in your group some of them can catch seats for you while you place order. Very low key place for fresh food. The options mainly seem to be based around variations of chappati. The tea ia really good there. Compared to other places this seemed to be the most crowded.

Considering the size of the coffeeshop itself , place is pretty productive and can handle many visitors at once. Plenty of seating areas outside with reasonable pricing and decent options. Staff members are quite nice and friendly. Tasty tea and chapati were had. Worth visiting again
Doha street food . The paratha with different stuffing .it's yummy ,easy to go , less time consuming and cost effective .

This eatery seems to be a favourite among the locals. It is frequently crowded, so be prepared to share a table with other diners if you visit during peak hours. The chapati here is great.

The one notable downside to keep in mind is the moderate amount of flies buzzing around the seating area, which can be quite distracting and takes away from the overall comfort of the meal.

This charming restaurant, nestled in the heart of the bustling souq, offers a true taste of tradition.  The menu boasts an array of familiar favorites, all prepared with care and authenticity.  From the perfectly blistered chapati to the rich, aromatic karak, each bite transports you to the heart of home-style cooking. The warm atmosphere and friendly service enhance the dining experience, making it a must-visit for anyone seeking a taste of comforting, traditional flavors.  Don't miss this gem on your next trip to the souq!
